pfd.utils.enc_categ_var module

pfd.utils.enc_categ_var.enc_categ_var(df: DataFrame, col: str, prefix: str, rm_first: bool, rm_categ_var: bool) → DataFrame[source]

Encode a categorical variable.

This function encodes a categorical variable to a one-hot integer array and concatenates it to the input DataFrame.

Parameters:

  • df (pd.DataFrame) – DataFrame with variables to be encoded.

  • col (str) – Variables to be encoded.

  • prefix (str) – String to prepend DataFrame column names.

  • rm_first (bool) – Whether to get k-1 dummies out of k categorical levels by removing the first level.

  • rm_categ_var (bool) – Whether to remove the input categorical variable after encoding.

Returns:

DataFrame with encoded variables.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

Examples

for ele in df.select_dtypes(include=[“category”]).columns:

df = enc_categ_var(df, ele, “_”, True, True)

pfd.utils.est_pm_mod module

pfd.utils.est_pm_mod.est_pm_mod(model: Model, seed: int, n_draws: int | None = None, n_tune: int | None = None, n_chains: int | None = None, n_cores: int | None = None, targ_acpt: float | None = None, vi: bool = False, vi_n_iter: int | None = None, vi_n_draws: int | None = None, *args: tuple, **kwargs: dict[str, Any]) → tuple[Any, Any, Any] | InferenceData[source]

Estimate PyMC model.

This function either numerically estimates the defined PyMC model using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo methods (NUTS) or approximates the results using Variational Inference.

Parameters:

  • model (pymc.Model) – PyMC model to be numerically estimated.

  • seed (int) – Random seed.

  • n_draws (int | None, default None) – Number of draws.

  • n_tune (int | None, default None) – Number of tuning samples (burn-in).

  • n_chains (int | None, default None) – Number of chains.

  • n_cores (int | None, default None) – Number of cores.

  • targ_acpt (float | None, default None) – Target acceptance rate.

  • vi (bool, default False) – Whether variational inference should be used for estimation.

  • vi_n_iter (int, default None) – Number of iterations for variational inference.

  • vi_n_draws (int, default None) – Number of draws for variational inference.

  • *args (tuple) – Parameters specific to the trace.

  • **kwargs (Dict[str, Any]) – Parameters specific to the trace.

Returns:

Record of the estimation process.

Return type:

Tuple[Any, Any, Any] | arviz.InferenceData

pfd.utils.write_text_file module

pfd.utils.write_text_file.write_text_file(file: str, body: str, first_line: int | None = 1, last_line: int | None = -1) → None[source]

Write text to a text file.

This function can be particulary useful to store TeX table code in a text file. For example, the first and the last line can be stripped to embed the file within a TeX tabular environment.

Parameters:

  • file (str) – Name (path) of file.

  • body (str) – Text to write.

  • first_line (int | None, default 1) – First line to write.

  • last_line (int | None, default -1) – Last line to write.

Return type:

None

See also

pandas.DataFrame.to_latex

Render object to a LaTeX tabular, longtable, or nested table.

Examples

>>> df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [1.5, 0.1234], "B": [-2, 15000]})
>>> df.head()
...
        A      B
0  1.5000     -2
1  0.1234  15000
>>> write_text_file(
        file="df.tex",
        body=df.to_latex(),
        first_line=1,
        last_line=-1
    )
